rich_description: Workfare Skills Support (WSS) is the training arm of the Workfare scheme, designed to help low-wage Singapore citizen workers upgrade their skills with minimal out-of-pocket cost. Eligible workers (income ≤ $2,500/month, citizen, aged 30+) receive (a) absentee payroll funding while attending approved courses, so they don't lose income for taking time off work, (b) up to 95% course-fee subsidy on SSG-approved courses on the SkillsFuture catalogue, and (c) a $200 training commitment cash award after completing a qualifying course. It also comes with a one-time SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of $4,000 for workers aged 40+. WSS works alongside the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) — the cash-and-CPF top-up paid quarterly to low-wage workers — but is a distinct programme focused on upskilling. If your household runs on a single low-wage breadwinner and they want to train into a better-paying role without losing the salary they currently bring in, this is the scheme designed for exactly that.

other_criteria: Monthly gross income at or below $2,500
Worked for at least 2 of the past 12 months (employed or self-employed)
Owns no more than one property; if married, household must not own more than 2 properties
Course must be on the SSG-approved SkillsFuture catalogue and aligned with the worker's Individual Learning Plan

required_documents.name: Recent payslips or CPF contribution history

oth_location: Apply via MySkillsFuture portal. The ServiceSG counter at Tampines OTH and the WSG Careers Connect coaches can assist with login, course selection, and Workfare eligibility checks. PLACEHOLDER — verify whether ServiceSG counter at OTH handles WSS-specific enquiries.
typical_processing_time: Course-fee subsidy applied at point of enrolment. Absentee payroll claim reimbursed to worker (or employer) within 8-12 weeks of course completion. $200 training commitment award disbursed within 4 weeks of completion.
